title: Population ecology
group: BIO-EVOL / BIO-ECOL / BIO-PLANT — Evolution, Ecology & Plants
examples: What is the difference between exponential and logistic growth?
How does carrying capacity affect a population over time?
Can a population ever exceed its carrying capacity?

explain.say: Today we are looking at how populations of living things change.
Exponential growth happens when resources are unlimited for a species.
The logistic curve shows growth that slows down over time.
Carrying capacity is the maximum population the environment can support.
When a population reaches carrying capacity, growth slows to zero.
In the real world, predator-prey cycles show logistic patterns.

faq.q: What is the difference between exponential and logistic growth?
faq.a: Exponential growth assumes unlimited resources, making the curve shoot up rapidly. Logistic growth is more realistic because it accounts for limited resources, forming an S-shape.
asks: When does a population grow fastest?

faq.q: How is carrying capacity determined in nature?
faq.a: Carrying capacity is determined by the limiting factors of the environment, such as available food or space. These factors set an upper limit on population size.

faq.q: Does a population ever go below its carrying capacity?
faq.a: Yes, a population can drop below carrying capacity due to disease or over-harvesting. However, it will tend to grow back towards K if conditions allow.

faq.q: Are there any situations where logistic growth is not accurate?
faq.a: Logistic growth is an average model; sudden environmental changes or catastrophic events can cause deviations. The model assumes relatively stable limiting factors.
asks: What if the environment changes suddenly?

faq.q: What are the main limiting factors for a population?
faq.a: The main limiting factors are usually food availability, space, water, or accumulation of waste products. These resources directly restrict how large the population can become.

facts: Exponential growth occurs when resources are unlimited.
The logistic growth curve forms an 'S' shape.
Carrying capacity (K) is the maximum population size an environment can sustain.
Limiting factors restrict population growth rates.

quiz.say: A population's growth rate is highest when:

options.show: The population is at half of the carrying capacity.
options.say: The population is at half of the carrying capacity.

options.show: When the population is at carrying capacity
options.say: When the population is at carrying capacity

options.show: When the population is very small
options.say: When the population is very small

options.show: When the population is growing exponentially
options.say: When the population is growing exponentially

quiz.why: At half the carrying capacity, the population has enough individuals to reproduce quickly, but resources have not yet become severely limited.

wrong.1: At K, the growth rate is zero because resources are fully depleted.
wrong.2: When the population is very small, the rate of reproduction is also low.
wrong.3: Exponential growth is unsustainable because it ignores limiting factors.

quiz.say: If the carrying capacity of a pond is 500 frogs, what happens when the population reaches 500?

options.show: The population will continue to grow exponentially.
options.say: The population will continue to grow exponentially.

options.show: The growth rate will approach zero.
options.say: The growth rate will approach zero.

quiz.why: Reaching K means the environment cannot support more individuals, causing the growth rate to level off.

wrong.0: Doubling would require unlimited resources, which is not the case at K.
wrong.1: A crash only happens if the environment suddenly becomes worse, not just by reaching K.
wrong.2: Exponential growth ignores the physical limits of the pond's resources.

quiz.say: Which curve best represents population growth limited by food supply?
quiz.why: The logistic curve naturally flattens out as it approaches the carrying capacity set by the food supply.

wrong.0: This curve suggests infinite resources, which is biologically impossible.
wrong.1: This suggests no change, even when the population is growing from a low number.
wrong.2: This suggests the population is always declining, which is not always true.
